rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-039 (illustrative figures), A-1: without the cap, pumping would stay near 300,000 af and above 210,000.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-039 (illustrative figures), A-2: the cap is enforced against most pumpers; meters, telemetry and satellite checks detect most over-pumping.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-039 (illustrative figures), A-10: detection is weak for some wells, so some pumpers over-pump.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-039 (illustrative figures), A-11: South growers, North communities and landholders without history can organize at a cost below their stake.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-039 (illustrative figures), A-3: holders expect shares to last, without early reallocation (shares are permanent; the 2032 review may scale them but not reassign them).
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-039 (illustrative figures), A-16: tree nuts earn more per af than field crops for most growers, so holders' values of an af differ.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-039 (illustrative figures), A-4: a lease market forms; transaction costs are low enough for holders to lease to others within a season.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-039 (illustrative figures), A-19: the fall in basin tree-nut output moves national tree-nut prices by more than a negligible amount (basin share about 5%); A-18 gives 0.15 for field crops.
